signals.title: USD/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Fed Hawkish Shift
signals.text: The US Dollar is outperforming all G10 peers as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers a hawkish tilt at Jackson Hole, reviving expectations for further tightening. EUR/USD has fallen sharply to 1.1609, testing the SMA20 support level at 1.1591 as the market reprices the Fed's stance. The 135bp carry advantage favored by the Fed's 3.75% rate versus the ECB's 2.4% is now reinforced by rising US 10Y yields, which have climbed to 4.69%. While the ECB's Dolenc has signaled arguments for a September hike, the immediate momentum is firmly with the USD as the bear-flattener yield curve regime signals dominant tightening expectations. Trade bias: Bullish USD/EUR; hawkish Fed rhetoric overrides moderate ECB hike pricing. Catalyst: ECB meeting 10 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: EUR/USD holds 1.1591 SMA20 support and Jackson Hole volatility fades without a concrete policy shift.

signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Crowded Long
signals.text: The AUD/CHF cross represents the most extreme divergence in the G10 complex this week with a 214bp performance spread. AUD is the clear leader, gaining 1.397% on average across peers, while CHF remains the laggard at -0.743% amid a risk-on environment and low VIX of 14.2. AUD/USD trades at 0.7178, well above its SMA20/50/200 cluster, supported by a 435bp carry premium against the SNB's 0.0% rate. However, COT data shows AUD speculative positioning is now crowded at a 94th percentile (z=+1.78), while retail sentiment is 94% short AUD/CHF, creating a heavy contrarian reversal risk if momentum stalls. Trade bias: Long AUD/CHF; carry-driven outperformance faces positioning-led exhaustion risk. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep. Risk: Sharp risk-off shift spikes VIX above 20, triggering a rapid unwind of the AUD carry trade.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Options Skew Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY is testing the critical 160.00 psychological level, currently at 159.96, as the 275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential remains the dominant driver. Despite the bullish price action, the options market is pricing significant downside protection, with the 1M 25d risk reversal at -1.81, a strong put skew. This divergence suggests institutional participants are hedging for potential BoJ intervention or a Jackson Hole-induced reversal even as the carry trade remains crowded with JPY net shorts at -73k (12th percentile). Real policy rates remain deeply accommodative for JPY at -0.90%, keeping the structural pressure on the yen until a hawkish BoJ shift is realized. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; carry-supportive while holding below 160.00 intervention risk. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: Confirmed BoJ intervention at 160.00 triggers a disorderly unwind of speculative shorts.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning + Volatility + ESI
signals.text: GBP/USD has tumbled to 1.3557 following hawkish Fed comments, but remains positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.3537/1.3418/1.3437. Speculative positioning in Sterling is highly crowded at a 92nd percentile (lev_net +46k, z+1.22), leaving the pair vulnerable to further profit-taking if US yields continue to climb. The options market is pricing in significant tail risk with a GBP/USD VRP of +6.1%, as IV at 11.0% sits far above the 4.9% realized volatility. This elevated premium, combined with a negative Economic Surprise Index of -9.3, suggests the 'Long GBP' consensus is being tested by both data disappointments and external dollar strength. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish GBP/USD; crowded longs face technical test of SMA20. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep. Risk: US 10Y yields retreat below 4.50%, easing the pressure on the GBP/USD carry neutrality.
